questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy arranges a sequence of transfers so that a patient ends up holding a supply the pharmacy could not lawfully have dispensed to him directly. Each transfer in the sequence, taken on its own, complies with the governing rules, and every step is documented. How should the arrangement be assessed?

choices.text: No violation arises, because each step in the sequence independently complies.
No violation arises, because the prohibition reaches only direct circumvention.
A violation arises if the Board shows the patient was harmed by the supply.
A violation arises if the pharmacy gained financially from the arrangement.
A violation arises, because the manner was designed to circumvent the law.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy has prescription pads printed with its own name and address and supplies them free of charge to a nearby prescriber. There is no agreement of any kind between them, nothing of value passes, and no patient is ever sent to the pharmacy as a result. What is the pharmacy's position?

choices.text: Compliant, because nothing of value passed to the prescriber.
Compliant, because no patient was in fact steered to the pharmacy.
Compliant, provided the prescriber stays free to send prescriptions elsewhere.
In violation, because supplying forms that refer to a pharmacy is prohibited.
In violation, but only where the forms are used for controlled substances.

questions.stem: An authorized pharmacist practising collaborative drug therapy management in a Massachusetts community pharmacy is asked during an inspection to produce the collaborative practice documents. Which statements about what this pharmacist is required to hold are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacist must hold the signed original rather than a copy.
A copy of the current collaborative practice agreement must be maintained.
Copies of the current patient referral and patient consent must be included.
The documents must be maintained in the primary practice setting.
The documents must be readily retrievable when they are requested.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts collaborating pharmacist keeps the required documents on site. An investigator from the Board of Registration in Medicine asks to see them and the pharmacist answers that they are retrievable only to the Board of Registration in Pharmacy. Separately, the supervising physician has handed the pharmacist the original agreement for safekeeping. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: The pharmacist is right on retrievability and right to hold the original.
The pharmacist is right on retrievability but should return the original.
The pharmacist is wrong on retrievability and right to hold the original.
Both boards may request the documents, and the physician may pass the original on.
Both boards may request them, and the original belongs in the physician's record.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts collaborating pharmacist wants an appropriately trained certified technician to collect the vital signs contemplated by her collaborative practice agreement. The agreement says nothing at all about delegation. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Silence in the agreement operates as permission to delegate the duty.
Delegation is permitted because the technician is appropriately trained.
Delegation is permitted because collecting vital signs is not a dispensing act.
The agreement must specify which of the pharmacist's duties may be delegated.
The agreement must specify which duties under it may not be delegated.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts collaborative practice agreement names three duties of the authorized pharmacist that may be delegated and two that may not. It says nothing further on the subject. The pharmacist proposes to delegate one of the named duties to trained staff for the next six weeks. What does the agreement still lack?

choices.text: Nothing further, once the delegable and non-delegable duties have been named.
Board approval of this particular delegation before it may take effect.
The when and how of delegation, together with its duration and its scope.
A separate written consent from the patient to the proposed delegation.
The supervising physician's countersignature on the delegation itself.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts retail pharmacy proposes to engage a physician on two footings: to conduct quality assurance reviews of the pharmacists it employs who practise collaborative drug therapy management, and to enter into collaborative practice agreements with the pharmacy's patients. Which analysis is correct?

choices.text: Both engagements are permitted, since the pharmacy is not itself prescribing.
Both engagements are prohibited, since a retail pharmacy may not employ a physician.
The agreement engagement is permitted and the review engagement is prohibited.
Both are permitted if the physician's pay is unrelated to prescription volume.
The review engagement is permitted and the agreement engagement is prohibited.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts community pharmacist is asked to begin collaboratively managing a walk-in who says her physician mentioned that the pharmacy could help with her blood pressure. Nothing is in writing and the pharmacist has had no contact with the physician. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: She is a collaborative patient because her own physician suggested it.
She is a collaborative patient because she has presented herself for the service.
The supervising physician must assess her and include a diagnosis on referral.
She becomes a collaborative patient once the pharmacist records the conversation.
In this setting she must be notified of and must consent to the services.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts supervising physician refers a patient for collaborative drug therapy management, records the referral and the patient's consent in his own chart, and tells the collaborating pharmacist that the documentation is complete and nothing further is needed. Where must the individual referral and consent be recorded?

choices.text: In the supervising physician's record alone, which is what the statute requires.
In the pharmacist's record alone, since the pharmacist delivers the service.
In whichever of the two records the professionals agree should hold them.
In the patient's record, by the pharmacist and by the supervising physician.
In a register filed with the Board, separately from the patient's record.

questions.stem: On the same morning a Massachusetts hospital pharmacist begins collaboratively managing an inpatient after a discussion about that patient with the attending supervising physician, and a community pharmacist begins collaboratively managing a walk-in after an identical discussion with her supervising physician. Neither holds a signed individual referral. Which analysis is correct?

choices.text: Both are properly referred, since a consultation is a referral in any setting.
The hospital pharmacist is properly referred; the community pharmacist is not.
The community pharmacist is properly referred; the hospital pharmacist is not.
Neither is properly referred, because a written referral is always required.
Neither is properly referred, because a referral must be signed to be effective.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is mapping out what a proposed collaborative practice agreement could cover. Which activities may fall within collaborative drug therapy management as the statute defines it? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Initiating, monitoring, modifying and discontinuing the patient's drug therapy.
Collecting and reviewing the patient's history.
Obtaining and checking pulse, temperature, blood pressure and respiration.
Settling a diagnosis where a laboratory result plainly supports one.
Ordering and evaluating laboratory tests directly related to the drug therapy.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts collaborating pharmacist orders a laboratory test directly related to the drug therapy she co-manages, under an approved protocol for her setting and in direct consultation with the supervising physician, and then evaluates the result. Her evaluation concludes that the patient has a new condition. What is the position?

choices.text: The ordering may be proper, but the evaluation may not include a diagnostic component.
The ordering is improper, because a pharmacist may not order laboratory tests.
Both are proper, because the test was directly related to the therapy managed.
Both are improper, because laboratory work sits outside collaborative management.
Both are proper, provided she reports the conclusion to the supervising physician.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts collaborative practice agreement will lapse at the end of this month and will not be renewed. The pharmacist plans to write to each affected patient in the week after the lapse, explaining that the arrangement has ended and how their therapy will be continued. Which duty has already been missed?

choices.text: None; written notice after the lapse discharges both of the duties owed.
Notice to the Board of Registration in Pharmacy in advance of the lapse.
Notice to each affected patient's other prescribers in advance of the lapse.
A written variation of the agreement extending it beyond the lapse date.
Arranging an uninterrupted continuation of therapy before the lapse.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts collaborating pharmacist holds two patient referrals. One is written in indelible pencil. The other arrived by email as a flattened image which the pharmacy system can neither store nor retrieve in readable form. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The pencil referral fails, because a paper document must be written in ink.
The emailed referral succeeds, because electronic transmission is permitted.
Both fail, because a referral must carry a handwritten signature to be valid.
The referral in indelible pencil satisfies the writing requirement.
The emailed referral fails the readable and retrievable requirement.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy delivers prescriptions to patients at their homes. With each parcel it encloses delivery paperwork printed with a toll-free number the patient may call to speak with the pharmacy's pharmacist. Nothing about the number appears on the medication containers themselves. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: Compliant, because the patient receives the toll-free number with the medication.
Compliant, because the offer to counsel may be made by any reasonable method.
Not compliant, because the number must be on a label affixed to each container.
Not compliant, because home delivery requires a face-to-face offer to counsel.
Not compliant, because a toll-free service cannot satisfy the counselling duty.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is asked about a dispensing from last year. Its records contain no entry that the patient failed to accept the pharmacist's offer to counsel, and no entry that counselling was actually given. What follows from that state of the records?

choices.text: Nothing follows; the records are simply silent about what happened that day.
A presumption arises that the counselling was provided to that patient.
A presumption arises that the counselling was not provided to that patient.
The pharmacy must instead produce the dispensing pharmacist's recollection.
The pharmacy is in breach, because counselling must be affirmatively recorded.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is reviewing a proposed collaborative practice agreement before signing it. Which features does the statutory definition require for the agreement to be validly constituted? Select all that apply.

choices.text: It must be written and signed by the pharmacist and the supervising physician.
The collaborative practice must sit within the supervising physician's practice.
It is subject to review and renewal on a biennial basis.
It must be filed with the Board before the pharmacist may act under it.
It must include individually developed guidelines for any prescriptive practice.

questions.stem: Two Massachusetts pharmacists reach opposite conclusions on the same drug utilization review question. One relies on a current peer-reviewed journal article that is not among the works named in the regulation. The other relies on a superseded edition of a compendium that is named. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The journal article is unacceptable, because the regulation does not name it.
The journal article may properly be relied upon as peer-reviewed literature.
Neither may be relied upon, since only the named works are acceptable sources.
The superseded edition remains acceptable, because the compendium is named.
The superseded edition fails, because the review must rest on current standards.

questions.stem: During prospective review a Massachusetts pharmacist identifies a therapeutic duplication, telephones the prescriber, agrees a change to the therapy, and dispenses the revised prescription. She makes no note of the call, on the basis that the clinical issue was fully resolved before anything was dispensed. What remains outstanding?

choices.text: Nothing; resolving the issue clinically discharges what the regulation requires.
A report of the therapeutic duplication to the Board of Registration in Pharmacy.
A second prospective review of the revised therapy before it is dispensed.
Written confirmation from the prescriber of the change that was agreed.
Documentation of the measures she took in response to the review.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts community pharmacy that holds the equipment and the ingredients turns away a request for a simple non-sterile oral suspension that is customary in its community, telling the parent it prefers not to compound. Later the same day it declines a request for a sterile preparation. How should the two refusals be assessed?

choices.text: Both are permitted, since compounding is a service a pharmacy may choose to offer.
Both are prohibited, since a licensee may not refuse to compound on preference.
The first refusal is permitted and the second refusal is prohibited on these facts.
The first refusal is prohibited and the second falls outside the duty entirely.
Both turn on whether another nearby pharmacy could have compounded them instead.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist arranges a dispensing record so that a reviewer will draw a conclusion the pharmacist knows to be untrue. Every individual entry is literally accurate, no dispensing rule is broken, and in the event no one relies on the record and no loss is suffered by anyone. What is the position?

choices.text: No violation, because every entry the pharmacist made is literally accurate.
No violation, because no separate dispensing rule was broken by the pharmacist.
A violation, because a licensee may not engage in any deceptive act.
A violation if the Board shows a reviewer actually relied on the arrangement.
A violation if the arrangement produced some financial gain for the pharmacy.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist discloses nothing about any patient to anyone. Completed prescriptions sit face up on an open counter and a printed waiting list showing patient names is visible to everyone standing in the queue. No one is shown to have read either of them. What is the position?

choices.text: Compliant, because the pharmacist made no disclosure to any third party.
Compliant, because no one is shown to have read the information on display.
Compliant, provided the pharmacy makes a private consultation area available.
In breach, but only once a patient complains about the arrangement.
In breach, because the duty includes protecting confidential information.

questions.stem: Two Massachusetts patients present returns at the same pharmacy on the same afternoon. The first was given the wrong strength by the pharmacy. The second simply changed therapy, and that product was correctly dispensed and is not defective. How must the pharmacy respond to the two returns?

choices.text: It must accept the first return and is not required to accept the second.
It must accept both returns, because the pharmacy dispensed both products.
It may decline both returns, because neither product can be dispensed again.
It must accept the second return and may decline the first for quarantine.
It must accept both, but may return only the second one to its inventory.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy supplies a naloxone rescue kit to one walk-in requestor and has none readily available when a second walk-in asks for one an hour later. Which statements about what the pharmacy owes are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Counselling must be provided to the first requestor at the time of dispensing.
The opioid antagonist information pamphlet must be provided at that same time.
The second requestor must be referred to the nearest location holding stock.
The second requestor may simply be invited to return another day.
The referral duty applies even though this pharmacy cannot supply the product.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is asked for naloxone by a woman who explains that she intends it for her adult son, who is not present. She does not ask to pay out of pocket. Whose insurance coverage should the pharmacy pursue, and at what point?

choices.text: The son's coverage, and the claim may be submitted after the product is supplied.
The son's coverage, and the claim must be submitted before it is supplied.
The mother's coverage, and the claim may be submitted after it is supplied.
The mother's coverage, and the claim must be submitted before it is supplied.
Neither, because a purchase intended for another person must be paid in cash.

questions.stem: At one Massachusetts pharmacy a patient refuses to give any allergy history after being asked on three separate visits. At another, a patient is never asked because the queue is long. Both patient profiles are incomplete in exactly the same respect. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Both pharmacies are compliant, because the standard is only reasonable effort.
Both pharmacies are in breach, because the profile has to be complete.
Compliance turns on whether the missing history was clinically significant.
The first pharmacy made a reasonable effort and is compliant on these facts.
The second pharmacy made no effort at all and is not compliant.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is directed by her employer to perform an administration technique that pharmacists in the Commonwealth are generally authorised to perform. She has never been trained in that technique and has never performed it. What governs her decision?

choices.text: She may proceed, because the act sits within the recognised pharmacist scope.
She may proceed, because her employer has directed her to perform it.
She may proceed if a colleague who is trained in it observes her doing it.
She may not proceed unless the Board grants her an individual authorisation.
She may not proceed, because it is outside her own training and experience.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist has been on duty for twelve hours when the relief pharmacist calls in sick and three patients are waiting on urgent therapy. Her district manager tells her to stay until the queue clears. Which statements about her continuing are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: She may continue only as an extenuating circumstance in the patient's interest.
The time she works beyond twelve hours must be minimized.
She must document the extenuating circumstance that justified continuing.
The manager's instruction is itself sufficient authority for her to continue.
The twelve hour ceiling is measured across a twenty-four hour period.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist properly worked fourteen hours yesterday under a documented extenuating circumstance. Since finishing she has rested four hours, worked a short shift in an unrelated setting, and then rested a further five hours. She now proposes to resume work in a pharmacy. What does the regulation require of her?

choices.text: Nothing further, since she has now rested nine hours in total since that shift.
An eight consecutive hour rest period before she resumes work in a pharmacy.
A twenty-four hour break, because the previous shift exceeded twelve hours.
Notification to the Board before she returns to practice in any pharmacy.
Nothing further, because the extenuating circumstance was properly documented.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is told by a colleague that the statutory prospective drug review is discharged once the screening items listed in the statute have been checked, and that it is owed only where the patient attends the pharmacy in person. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The listed screening items define the whole of the pharmacist's review duty.
The review is owed only where the patient attends the pharmacy in person.
The review is owed before each new prescription is dispensed or delivered.
The listed screening items are permissive rather than an exhaustive list.
Interactions with over-the-counter drugs fall outside the statutory review.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist has completed no training programme of any kind. She proposes to dispense emergency contraception under the statewide standing order this week, and to dispense a COVID-19 drug under a standing order next week. How do the two proposals compare?

choices.text: The emergency contraception dispensing may proceed; the COVID-19 drug may not.
The COVID-19 dispensing may proceed; the emergency contraception may not.
Both may proceed, because training is a professional expectation rather than a bar.
Neither may proceed, because both regimes require approved training beforehand.
Both may proceed once she notifies the Department that she intends to dispense.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy clearing expired stock offers it in three directions: to a licensed reverse distributor, to a volunteer overseas aid group that is not licensed to receive drugs, and to one of its own technicians who wants it for training purposes. Which of the transfers may lawfully proceed?

choices.text: All three, because expired stock is no longer a dispensable medicine at all.
All three, provided each recipient is told that the product has expired.
The transfer to the licensed reverse distributor, and neither of the other two.
The transfers to the reverse distributor and the aid group, but not the third.
None of them, because expired stock may never leave the pharmacy's custody.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy follows the edition of a United States Pharmacopeia chapter that has sat in its binder for years, on a practice point the Board has never regulated. On a second point it follows the current USP chapter although a Board regulation addresses that point differently. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The first practice is compliant, because a genuine USP chapter was followed.
The second practice is compliant, because USP is the recognised professional standard.
Neither point is governed by USP, since the Board has not adopted those chapters.
The first practice fails, because the most current USP chapter is the one that governs.
The second practice fails, because the Board regulation displaces USP on that point.

Record your selected choice IDs and your reasoning, then commit the Phase-1 lock. Do not open data/questions/, data/rules/, the authoring report, the post-lock reveal, the generated site payload, the controller ledger, the plan issue or any git history for these questions before that lock is committed.
content_boundary: Contains only question ID, type, stem and choices plus non-substantive package identity metadata. Excludes keyed answers, explanations, choice analysis, rule and drug identifiers, area, topic, subtopic, difficulty, family, provenance and all author reasoning.
